gen-eater-gf-rambla: Spiky and a bit sinister, with gaps between the letters. Rambla follows in small lowercase that nearly match its capitals, which leaves the whole pairing feeling cleanly grounded against the heading's menace.
gen-eater-gf-recursive: Menacing Eater draws thin strokes that look sharp but never brittle, while Recursive keeps one uniform line, like ballpoint ink. Dark up top, friendly below.
gen-eater-gf-roboto-condensed: Aggressive in mood but restrained in its contrast, Eater leads with a moody, gapped look, and Roboto Condensed glides beneath like drawn wire. Use the heading at large sizes.
gen-eater-gf-secular-one: Heavy-bodied and blunt, Secular One has no thick-thin swing at all. Eater gives the headline a restrained thick-thin rhythm, so a large heading size lets its gaps breathe while the body stays compact.
gen-eater-gf-tiny5: Tiny5 has short-looking ascenders because its body is so large, and it sits quietly under the heading. And Eater supplies the menace, its arches thinning slowly into slightly lighter joins.
gen-eater-gf-truculenta: Eater brings a dark, spaced-out look with a sensible thick-thin difference between strokes. And Truculenta packs into a compact line of rounded, open forms that moves along like fine rope.
gen-eater-gf-viga: Eater's horizontals run slightly slimmer than its verticals, giving it a dark bite. If the heading shrinks or Viga grows, that menace fades and its single stroke width starts to dominate.
gen-eater-gf-voces: Eater's dark, wide-set letters with short ascenders give it a menacing edge. Voces reads steadily in sans form, its stems and hairlines close in weight.
gen-eater-gf-winky-rough: Eater is dark and gap-toothed. Winky Rough sits beneath with a body height almost matching its capitals, while the heading's modest weight gap keeps its aggression in check.
gen-eater-gf-winky-sans: Winky Sans keeps its capitals barely taller than its lowercase, giving a modern, level look. And Eater, with a soft step from heavy to light strokes, belongs at display sizes in short lines.
